definitions.type: compact additive group with normalized measure
definitions.definition: torus=ℝ/(2πℤ), written \mathbb T in formulas; integration uses dx/(2π). The parameter T denotes the time horizon.

definitions.type: Fourier coefficient map on the torus
definitions.definition: For integrable f, Fourier(f)(k) = fhat(k) = (2 pi)^(-1) integral_0^{2 pi} f(x) exp(-ikx) dx; extend by distributional duality.

For real s, H^s is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with norm squared sum_{k in Z} <k>^(2s)|fhat(k)|^2, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). Negative spaces are distributions. L2=H^0 with normalized measure. On mean-zero distributions dot H^s has squared norm sum_{k!=0}|k|^(2s)|fhat(k)|^2. Smooth means spatially C-infinity. Real means fhat(-k)=conjugate(fhat(k)), and mean-zero means fhat(0)=0. Sequence ell2 uses counting measure. Time L-infinity norms are essential suprema, except time suprema of continuous representatives. Generic constants C may change; C_M depends only on gamma,T,M, never on a Fourier support bound or timestep.

definitions.type: Airy group indexed by real times
definitions.definition: S_t = exp(-t partial_x^3); Fourier(S_t f)(k)= exp(it k^3) fhat(k).
P0 f=fhat(0), as a constant function.
P=I-P0; the identity operator is I.

definitions.type: inverse spatial derivative with zero mode removed
definitions.definition: Dinv=partial_x^(-1)=D^(-1), Fourier multiplier (ik)^(-1) at nonzero k and zero at k=0.
Dinv2=D^(-2)=Dinv composed with Dinv.

definitions.type: quadratic increment, for positive tau and L2 inputs
definitions.definition: F_\tau(f)&=\tfrac16 P[(S_\tau D^{-1}f)^2]-\tfrac16 S_\tau P[(D^{-1}f)^2],\\

definitions.type: cubic increment, for positive tau and L2 inputs
definitions.definition:
H_\tau(f)&=\tfrac13 P[(S_\tau D^{-1}f)D^{-1}F_\tau(f)]
+\tfrac{\tau}{9}(S_\tau D^{-1}f)P_0(f^2)\\
&\quad-\tfrac1{54}\left[S_{\tau-s}D^{-1}[(S_sD^{-1}f)^3]\right]_{s=0}^{s=\tau}\\
&\quad-\tfrac1{27\tau}\left[S_{\tau-s}D^{-2}[(S_{s-\tau}D^{-2}F_\tau(f))(S_sD^{-1}f)]\right]_{s=0}^{s=\tau}.

definitions.type: one-step update and its finite iterates
definitions.definition: Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+F_tau(f)+H_tau(f) for tau>0. For any initial datum g0 and positive integer L with tau=T/L, set t_n=n tau, u_{g0}^0=g0, u_{g0}^{n+1}=Psi_tau(u_{g0}^n) for 0<=n<L, and v_{g0}^n=S_{-t_n}u_{g0}^n. Suppress the subscript g0 for the datum under discussion, using g0=u0 in the target. There is no spatial projection in Psi.
M_tau(g)=tau^(-1) integral_0^tau g(s) ds for tau>0.

\eta_\tau(\alpha,\beta)=M_\tau(e^{-is(\alpha+\beta)})
-M_\tau(e^{-is\alpha})M_\tau(e^{-is\beta}).

definitions.type: averaged cubic remainder on mean-zero polynomials, subsequently extended
definitions.definition: R2 = R^n_{2,tau}. For tau>0, real t_n and mean-zero polynomial f1,f2,f3, its output at k=0 is zero, and at k!=0 is -tau/(18 i k) sum_{a+b+c=k,a+b!=0} exp(-i t_n Phi) eta_tau(alpha,beta) f1hat(a) f2hat(b) f3hat(c), where p=a+b, alpha=3abp, beta=3kcp, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. The polynomial definition grants no bounded extension; a bounded extension must be proved separately.
B_t(f,g)=mathcal B_t(f,g)=S_{-t} partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)].
J_t(f,g)=mathcal J_t(f,g)=S_{-t}P[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].

definitions.type: time-integrated trilinear operator initially on smooth inputs
definitions.definition: C_I(f,g,h)= integral_I S_{-t}P{P[(S_t f)(S_t g)](S_t Dinv h)} dt. For lower regularity its meaning is the bounded extension supplied by the continuous estimates.

For compact interval I, ||f||_{X(I)}=||f||_{L-infinity(I;L2)}+||partial_t f||_{L-infinity(I;H^(-pstar))}, using the distributional time derivative. Subintervals use the same continuous representatives; piecewise smooth continuous functions have this distributional derivative almost everywhere.
a_gamma=1/2-gamma if 0<gamma<1/2, a_gamma=1/8 if gamma=1/2, and a_gamma=0 if 1/2<gamma<=1.
For time-independent mean-zero f and t in I_n=[t_n,t_n+tau], F_n(t;f)=1/2 integral_{t_n}^t B_s(f,f) ds. Write F_n(t)=F_n(t;f) when f is fixed.
z_n(t)=f+F_n(t;f).
C_n(t;f)=integral_{t_n}^t B_s(f,F_n(s;f)) ds.
Q_n(t;f)=1/2 integral_{t_n}^t B_s(F_n(s;f),F_n(s;f)) ds.
W_n(f)=Q_n(t_n+tau;f)+R^n_{2,tau}(f,f,f).

definitions.type: piecewise numerical interpolation, initially for smooth data
definitions.definition: For any smooth mean-zero step input f, time t_n and tau>0, define the step interpolation V(t;f)=f+F_n(t;f)+C_n(t;f)+Q_n(t;f)-(t-t_n)W_n(f)/tau on [t_n,t_n+tau]. On a numerical trajectory write V(t)=V(t;v^n) with f=v^n on I_n. Agreement of adjacent pieces is a proved property, not part of the definition.
For a step input f, Y_n(t;f)=V(t;f)-z_n(t;f); along a trajectory take f=v^n and suppress the input.

\rho_n(t)=-\int_{t_n}^t\mathcal B_s(Y_n,z_n)\,ds
-\tfrac12\int_{t_n}^t\mathcal B_s(Y_n,Y_n)\,ds
-\frac{t-t_n}{\tau}W_n.
Res=mathcal R, Res(0)=0 and Res(t)=sum_{j<n}rho_j(t_{j+1})+rho_n(t) on I_n, with the stage input f=v^j in each increment.

inputs.statement: For every I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b and b-a<=1, and fj in X(I), ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C|I| product_j||fj||_X+C||fi||_{L-infinity H^(-pstar)} product_{j!=i}||fj||_{L-infinity L2}, each i=1,2,3. For time-independent fj in H^lambda, 0<=lambda<=1, ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_lambda |I|^lambda product_j||fj||_{H^lambda}. At a=b the integral is zero. These are bounded extensions from smooth inputs and apply to continuous piecewise time-smooth inputs. For mean-zero w with ||w||_{H^gamma}<=M and 0<tau<=1, sup_{I_n}||F_n(t;w)||_{H^{a_gamma}}<=C_M tau^gamma and sup_{I_n}||F_n(t;w)||_{H^{1+gamma}}<=C_M. Also ||fg||_2<=C_gamma||f||_{H^gamma}||g||_{H^{a_gamma}}. Constants are uniform in step location and Fourier support.

For all real t and mean-zero L2 f,g, ||Dinv f||_{H^1}+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2, ||B_t(f,g)||_{H^(-pstar)}<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_{H^1}<=C||f||_2||g||_2 and ||J_t(f,g)||_2<=C||Dinv f||_2||g||_2. For L2 F,G, ||Dinv P(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2. For mean-zero A with Dinv A in L2, ||A||_{H^(-pstar)}<=||Dinv A||_2. H^1 is an algebra with product norm <=C product of norms. S_t is a Sobolev isometry preserving reality and mean. Projections P_{<=N}, P_{>N} contract Sobolev norms and X, and for s>=s0,N>=1, ||P_{>N}f||_{H^{s0}}<=C N^(s0-s)||f||_{H^s}, ||P_{<=N}f||_{H^s}<=C N^(s-s0)||f||_{H^{s0}}. For smooth mean-zero time-dependent f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. J is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=C_I(f,g,h). The identities hold for continuous piecewise time-smooth inputs by summing pieces.

inputs.statement: For any smooth real mean-zero initial datum g0, with all iterates initialized by g0, and positive integer L with tau=T/L>0, scheme iterates are smooth real and mean-zero. V is continuous on [0,T], spatially smooth and piecewise time-smooth, and V(t_n)=v^n=S_{-t_n}u^n. On every step f=v^n, v^{n+1}=f+F_n(t_{n+1})+C_n(t_{n+1})-R^n_{2,tau}(f,f,f). Moreover F_n'=B_t(f,f)/2, V'=B_t(z_n,z_n)/2-W_n/tau, Y_n'=B_t(f,F_n)+B_t(F_n,F_n)/2-W_n/tau, and Y_n(t_n)=0.

For smooth mean-zero f,w on I_n=[t_n,t_n+tau], t_n>=0, 0<tau<=1, ||w||_{H^gamma}<=M, delta_n=||f-w||_2<=1, q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n, form F_n,z_n,C_n,Q_n,W_n,V,Y_n by the step formulas with input f. Uniformly on I_n, ||F_n||_{H^1}<=C_M, ||F_n-F_n(.;w)||_{H^1}<=C_M delta_n, ||F_n||_{H^{a_gamma}}+||F_n||_2<=C_M q_n, ||z_n||_X<=C_M; ||B_t(F_n,F_n)||_2<=C_M q_n and sup||Q_n||_2+||W_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n; sup||Dinv B_t(f,F_n)||_2<=C_M q_n; sup||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n and sup||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=C_M q_n; sup||Y_n||_2<=C_M q_n, ||Y_n||_X<=C_M q_n and sup||Y_n||_{H^(-pstar)}<=C_M tau q_n. Exactly C_n(t)=(1/3)J_t(f,F_n(t))-(1/6)C_[t_n,t](f,f,f). No numerical Sobolev bound is required.

output.statement: For any smooth numerical trajectory, Res is continuous piecewise smooth, Res(0)=0, V'=B_t(V,V)/2+Res', and on each step Res'=-B_t(Y_n,z_n)-B_t(Y_n,Y_n)/2-W_n/tau. When comparison w=v(t_n) has H^gamma norm <=M, delta_n=||v^n-w||_2<=1, 0<tau<=1, q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n, sup_{I_n}||rho_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n and ||Res'||_{L-infinity(I_n;H^(-pstar))}<=C_M q_n. These estimates include every partial step endpoint.

Set f=v^n, the numerical twisted iterate on the current step.

Fix an arbitrary real M; the norm bound is imposed in L1.
Set w_perp=P w, removing only the zero Fourier mode.

argument.text: Fix any smooth numerical trajectory as in N007 and an arbitrary step n, with its positive timestep tau, t_n=n tau, I_n=[t_n,t_n+tau], f=v^n, and t in I_n. No comparison assumption is made in this paragraph. N007 gives smooth mean-zero f, continuity and piecewise smoothness of V, Y_n(t_n)=0, F_n'=B_t(f,f)/2 and V'=B_t(z_n,z_n)/2-W_n/tau. Hence z_n'=B_t(f,f)/2. Every B output has zero Fourier mode, since the spatial derivative in D017 kills that mode and S preserves it. Thus the integrals defining F_n,C_n,Q_n have mean zero. R2 has zero output mode by D014, so W_n, V, z_n and Y_n, and their stepwise derivatives, have mean zero as well. All these stages are smooth on each step. In D029 both integrals and the affine term vanish at t_n, so rho_n(t_n)=0. Integrating continuous smooth-stage integrands gives stepwise smooth rho_n, with derivative -B_t(Y_n,z_n)-B_t(Y_n,Y_n)/2-W_n/tau. In the finite concatenation D030, the value at each new left endpoint equals the preceding endpoint value, because the new increment starts at zero. Therefore Res is continuous, piecewise smooth and Res(0)=0. Its distributional derivative equals the stepwise derivative, since adjacent boundary terms cancel and there are no jumps. Symmetry and bilinearity of B follow directly from D017. Expanding V=z_n+Y_n in B_t(V,V) and using the displayed formula for V' proves V'=B_t(V,V)/2+Res' on each step, hence almost everywhere globally.

produces.statement: Without comparison conditions, Res is continuous piecewise smooth, Res(0)=0, V'=B_t(V,V)/2+Res', and Res'=-B_t(Y_n,z_n)-B_t(Y_n,Y_n)/2-W_n/tau on each step (and a.e. globally). The current f and stages z_n,Y_n and their stepwise derivatives are smooth mean-zero; Y_n(t_n)=0 and z_n'=B_t(f,f)/2.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary v and M in the output's domains and set w=v(t_n), delta_n=||f-w||_2 and q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n. Introduce L1: ||w||_{H^gamma}<=M, delta_n<=1 and 0<tau<=1. Smoothness of v makes w smooth. H001 gives 0<gamma<=1. We do not require w to have mean zero. Define w_perp=P w, delta_perp=||f-w_perp||_2 and q_perp=tau^gamma+delta_perp. From D005-D006, Fourier(w_perp)(0)=0 and Fourier(w_perp)(k)=Fourier(w)(k) for k!=0. Subtracting the constant P0 w preserves smoothness. The nonnegative Fourier summands in D003 give ||w_perp||_{H^gamma}^2=sum_{k!=0}<k>^(2gamma)|Fourier(w)(k)|^2<=||w||_{H^gamma}^2<=M^2. In particular ||w_perp||_{H^gamma}<=M, since L1 implies M>=0. By F001, Fourier(f)(0)=0 and P f=f. Consequently f-w_perp=P(f-w), and delta_perp^2=sum_{k!=0}|Fourier(f-w)(k)|^2<=delta_n^2, so delta_perp<=delta_n<=1. Thus 0<q_perp<=q_n<=2; the last inequality uses 0<tau^gamma<=1. The grid has t_n>=0. Apply N008 with its two spatial inputs equal to f and w_perp, its error equal to delta_perp and its control quantity equal to q_perp. All its smoothness, mean-zero, time, norm and error premises have now been verified. The stages in its conclusion are exactly the original stages: their formulas depend on f, t_n and tau, not on the comparison. Replacing q_perp by the larger q_n in the nonnegative bounds gives ||z_n||_X<=C_M, sup||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n, sup||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=C_M q_n, sup||Y_n||_2+||Y_n||_X<=C_M q_n, sup||Y_n||_{H^(-pstar)}<=C_M tau q_n and ||W_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n on I_n. Also ||f||_2<=||w||_2+delta_n<=M+1, because the H^gamma Fourier weights are at least one. Since f is time-independent, its X norm on every subinterval is ||f||_2<=M+1. Restrictions cannot increase any of these suprema or X norms.

produces.statement: Under L1, 0<q_n<=2, ||f||_2<=M+1, and the time-constant f has X norm <=M+1 on every subinterval of I_n. On I_n, ||z_n||_X<=C_M, sup||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n, sup||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=C_M q_n, sup||Y_n||_2+||Y_n||_X<=C_M q_n, sup||Y_n||_{H^(-pstar)}<=C_M tau q_n, and ||W_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n. All these bounds restrict to every partial step with the same constants.

argument.text: Continue under L1 and let t be any point of I_n. Apply N006's integration-by-parts identity to (Y_n,z_n) on [t_n,t]; F001 supplies smooth mean-zero inputs and Y_n(t_n)=0. It yields integral_{t_n}^t B_s(Y_n,z_n) ds=(1/3)J_t(Y_n(t),z_n(t))-(1/3)integral_{t_n}^t J_s(Y_n',z_n) ds-(1/6)C_[t_n,t](f,f,Y_n). Here z_n'=B_s(f,f)/2, symmetry of J and the J(B(f,f),Y_n) identity in N006 give the last term. By N006's estimate ||J_s(A,G)||_2<=C||Dinv A||_2||G||_2 and F002, the endpoint is bounded by C_M tau q_n and the first derivative integral by C_M (t-t_n)q_n<=C_M tau q_n. For the trilinear term instantiate N005 on [t_n,t] with (f1,f2,f3)=(f,f,Y_n) and i=3. This interval has nonnegative left endpoint and length at most tau<=1. F002 verifies membership in X and bounds the right side by C_M[(t-t_n)q_n+tau q_n]<=C_M tau q_n. At t=t_n the integral is zero by definition. For the second integral in rho_n, N006 with (Y_n,Y_n) gives integral_{t_n}^t B_s(Y_n,Y_n) ds=(1/3)J_t(Y_n(t),Y_n(t))-(2/3)integral_{t_n}^t J_s(Y_n',Y_n) ds. Its endpoint has norm <=C_M(tau q_n)q_n, and its derivative integral has norm <=C_M(t-t_n)q_n^2, again by the Dinv estimate and F002. Thus this whole integral is bounded by C_M tau q_n^2<=2 C_M tau q_n. Finally ||(t-t_n)W_n/tau||_2<=||W_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n. Taking the triangle inequality in D029 proves ||rho_n(t)||_2<=C_M tau q_n. The constant is independent of t, so the estimate holds uniformly at every partial endpoint.

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_{t in I_n}||rho_n(t)||_2<=C_M tau q_n, including every partial step endpoint.

argument.text: Under L1, the derivative formula in F001 and N006's B estimate, applied to the smooth mean-zero pairs (Y_n,z_n) and (Y_n,Y_n), give ||Res'||_{H^(-pstar)}<=C||Y_n||_2||z_n||_2+C||Y_n||_2^2+||W_n||_{H^(-pstar)}/tau almost everywhere on I_n. Since pstar=23/14>0, D003's negative Sobolev weights are at most one, and ||W_n||_{H^(-pstar)}<=||W_n||_2. F002 therefore bounds the right side by C_M(q_n+q_n^2)+C_M q_n<=C_M q_n, after increasing the generic constant and using q_n<=2. Taking the essential supremum proves the required L-infinity negative Sobolev bound. Together with F003 this gives both quantitative conclusions. Discharge L1 into precisely the output's comparison antecedent, retaining the original w=v(t_n), delta_n and q_n. Universal introduction for the arbitrary comparison and step gives the conditional estimates in the output. F001 already proves the residual regularity, initial value and identities without L1. These unconditional conclusions and the discharged estimates together establish the unchanged output.
